A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same contrastive binary-code representation work, renamed from COMBO to CONTRABIN and substantially revised. Text, equations, figures and tables are readable throughout. Both documents end with references and contain no appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original pretraining validation losses and evaluations on POJ-104, BinaryCorp-3M and CGD/SeVC in Tables V–VIII.

after.justification: V2 reports original functionality classification, function-name recovery, summarization, reverse-engineering and ablation results in Tables 3–7, alongside embedding analyses and generation case studies.

M1.justification: V1 shares an encoder between source and binary code and uses a separate comment encoder. V2 instead shares a frozen encoder between source code and comments and trains a separate binary-code encoder. Section 2.1 and Algorithm 1 explicitly change parameter updating, making this a substantive architectural and training change beyond renaming.

E1.justification: V2 retains AnghaBench pretraining and LLVM-based POJ-104 classification, but removes BinaryCorp-3M x86 similarity and CGD/SeVC vulnerability evaluations. It adds function-name recovery using a repository-derived corpus called DIRT/DIRE in the document, plus summarization and binary-to-source generation using held-out AnghaBench data.

E2.justification: The retained POJ-104 comparison still evaluates RoBERTa, CodeBERT and GraphCodeBERT. However, COMBO-Light, which includes all three training stages, is replaced by CONTRABIN(PCL), trained with primary contrastive learning only. This changes an internal comparator substantively; DIRE/DIRTY are discussed for data provenance rather than evaluated as competing methods.

E3.justification: V2 introduces 91-way classification after function-name stripping and sequence-generation protocols with beam search and text-generation metrics. It specifies 10/30/30 pretraining epochs for comprehension while retaining 10/10/10 for analysis, plus task-specific generation budgets. POJ-104 fine-tuning hyperparameters remain unchanged; different tabulated sample counts alone do not establish that its experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V1's staged validation-loss and lightweight-model analysis is replaced by primary-only comparisons and explicit ablations removing comments, unfreezing the anchored encoder, or eliminating interpolation (v2 Table 7). V2 adds t-SNE embedding analysis and summarization/decompilation case studies (Figures 6–8). V1's cross-optimization and candidate-pool analyses disappear.

E5.justification: Both versions report fixed seeds, including 42 for pretraining and 123456 for POJ-104 fine-tuning. Neither reports repeated-run aggregation, confidence intervals, error bars or significance testing. V2's additional experiments continue the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: POJ-104 results are replaced: COMBO MAP is 0.737 in v1 Table VI, whereas CONTRABIN MAP is 43.78 in v2 Table 3. The model and reported sample counts differ, preventing a same-setting performance comparison. Similarity, vulnerability and stage-loss results disappear; recovery, generation and ablation results are added. V2 Table 6 gives GraphCodeBERT higher BLEU than CONTRABIN, 71.56 versus 71.14.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(3) revise the formal embedding maps and cross-similarity definitions to distinguish anchored source/comment representations from trainable binary representations. The interpolation and cross-entropy expressions retain their mathematical form, and no theorem or proof is added. The mathematical revision is limited to formalizing the changed model.

C1.justification: The central novelty claim about combining source code, binaries and comments through contrastive learning remains. However, the claimed empirical contribution is substantially redefined: v1's classification, similarity and vulnerability results and 5.45% average-improvement claim are replaced by claims covering classification, name recovery, summarization and reverse engineering, explicitly extending the contribution to binary-code comprehension.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations about harmful binary-driven updates to source/comment encoders, PCL overfitting, and semantic consistency in generated outputs. It removes v1's interpretations across x86, LLVM and source-code inputs and its substantive discussion of corpus diversity, representation choice, training capacity and plain-text-only limitations. These are changes in scientific interpretation and qualification, not relocation.

D1.justification: V2 documents a modified GHCC-to-LLVM collection pipeline, frequent-name filtering and anonymization, held-out AnghaBench preparation, input truncation, output lengths, beam size and generation budgets. These replace instructions for the removed experiments. Table 2 also supplies smaller POJ-104 sample counts, although both versions already describe excluding uncompilable examples, leaving actual resampling versus fuller disclosure unresolved.

R1.justification: V2 removes the dedicated simplex-interpolation/MixUp and graph-representation surveys, along with discussions of jTrans and BugGraph. It adds references concerning decompiled identifier naming, variable names and types, AnghaBench, t-SNE and generation metrics. This substantially changes the literature coverage and positioning toward binary comprehension, beyond reference renumbering.

P1.justification: Beyond renaming COMBO to CONTRABIN, v2 rewrites the abstract and introduction, moves related work from before the approach to after the results, reorganizes the research questions and results, and removes the standalone discussion/future-work section. Added boxed learning analogies and revised method explanations substantially change the narrative structure.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the architecture around frozen and trainable encoders, removes the separate primary-learning diagram, adds embedding and generation-case figures, and replaces much of the table suite. Results tables gain relative-change annotations and dataset statistics are consolidated. The journal template also changes typography, headers, author placement and page layout.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens component validation through Table 7's ablations and adds concrete generation examples. However, it removes v1's large-scale x86 cross-optimization evidence and substantive limitations discussion, while Section 4.1 treats a t-SNE visualization as proof of embedding quality. Better targeted validation therefore coexists with weaker support and qualification for broad applicability; the net effect on overall paper quality is not reliably assessable.
